parsed.attack: The professional's incentive is inverted: a landlord holding model numbers and the parts that fit them is a landlord who sources his own parts, challenges the quote and shops the next callout, so the plumber is being asked to hand out, unprompted and for free, the thing that erodes his own pricing power. The founder's own kill line requires 15 of 50 trades to pass it on unprompted within four weeks - a 30% unpaid-marketer rate no product achieves without a spiff, and a freemium subscription at this ARPU cannot fund one. Cycle time compounds it: a single-unit landlord meets a trade perhaps twice a year, so even a willing referrer turns the loop on a six-month clock, against a rule where a 3-day loop beats a stronger 30-day one.
parsed.strongest_defence: A minority of trades actively want the record to exist, because arriving at a documented boiler saves them an unbilled diagnostic visit, and the better channel is the landlord's own peers - NRLA forums, r/uklandlords, local landlord association meetings - where 'what have I actually got installed' is a daily post and this is the one-line answer, shared by someone with the same single flat.
parsed.verdict_reason: The named referrer loses pricing power by referring and meets the user twice a year, so the professional loop cannot reach the 30% unprompted pass-on rate the plan assumes.
